statement_nl: Step A1 proves the theorem for n = 2. Steps A2-A15 establish the strong inductive step from all smaller sizes to an arbitrary n >= 3. Therefore, for every integer n >= 2, if f(s) denotes the number of permutations (a_1,...,a_n) of {1,...,n} such that s_i * (a_{i+1} - a_i) > 0 for all i, then the sequences s for which f(s) is maximal are exactly the alternating sign sequences, equivalently those satisfying s_i * s_{i+1} = -1 for every 1 <= i <= n-2.
